questions.question: Who proposed and created Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) in 1994?
questions.hint: Norwegian web pioneer who worked with Tim Berners-Lee at CERN.
questions.explanation: Håkon Wium Lie proposed CSS in 1994 while working with Tim Berners-Lee at CERN.

questions.question: Which method of applying CSS is recommended for production multi-page web applications?
options: Inline style attributes on every HTML tag
External stylesheet linked via <link rel="stylesheet"> in <head>
Internal <style> tags at the bottom of the body
questions.hint: External stylesheets can be cached across all pages.
questions.explanation: External stylesheets promote separation of concerns, code reusability, and browser caching across multiple pages.

questions.question: What is Flash of Unstyled Content (FOUC)?
options: A brief visual glitch where a webpage is shown in raw unstyled HTML before stylesheets load
questions.hint: Unstyled content flashing before styles apply.
questions.explanation: FOUC happens when stylesheets load late, causing unstyled text to briefly flash on screen before visual styles apply.

questions.question: Which phase of the browser rendering pipeline calculates the exact physical coordinates and dimensions of elements?
questions.explanation: The Layout (or Reflow) phase calculates the geometric coordinates, widths, and heights of elements in the render tree.

questions.question: Why can pseudo-classes like :hover and media queries NOT be used with inline styles?
options: Inline styles only accept declarations for the current element state and cannot express selectors or at-rules
Inline styles only support black and white colors
Inline styles are limited to 10 characters
questions.hint: Inline styles have no selector block.
questions.explanation: Inline style attributes only accept property-value pairs for the static element state and cannot express conditional pseudo-states or media queries.
